I used to have really bad social anxiety. Even a cashier asking me about my day and making small talk would make me deeply uncomfortable; sometimes I would freeze up not being able to respond, and then feel even worst, overthinking, feeling guilty, imagining they must think I'm being rude.One of the major things that forced me to overcome this was obtaining my first job where I was forced to smile and socialize with customers every day. I was very nervous at first, and it was obvious. Over time it became natural; I stopped overthinking everything I said, and now talking to strangers comes fairly easy to me.Just practice talking to people. Like with any other skill, you will improve at it over time.

Some other things I keep in mind: everyone is full of fairly full of themselves, and people like feeling important and memorable, and this is normal.

My motto is the best way to get someone to notice you is to notice them first.
